trust_decision.summary: An authority's stored acme_url is fetched server-side at certificate issuance (ClientV2.get_directory), so any value written to Authority.options.acme_url must be https and in ACME_DIRECTORY_HOST_ALLOWLIST before it is persisted. The published fix decides this at authorities.service.update, i.e. the PUT /api/1/authorities/<id> path, and exports the existing creation-time validator from the ACME issuer plugin so the update path can call it.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says the PUT update path stores options verbatim with no re-validation, so an engineer looks first at the 'if options:' block of authorities.service.update, where authority.options is assigned.

fix_sites.module_kind: service layer behind the REST handler

fix_sites.entry_point: helper used by both ACME create_authority implementations and now by authorities.service.update

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lemur/authorities/service.py:49-62 (authorities.service.update_options writes authority.options with no validation)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: update_options is an internal helper that Lemur itself calls (lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/acme_handlers.py:237) with the authority's own already-stored options, so it carries no user input and is not a route the advisory's PUT attack can reach.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing authorities (and the ACME_DIRECTORY_URL config fallback) may legitimately hold an acme_url whose host is not in the allowlist; the validator docstring records that they are deliberately not re-validated. A fix that moves the check to the fetch site would break certificate issuance for every such authority - the test config itself points at https://acme-v01.api.letsencrypt.org, which is not in the default allowlist.

O6_input_shapes: options supplied as a JSON string whose value is a list of {name, value} objects (the shape AuthorityUpdateSchema declares at lemur/authorities/schemas.py:101)
several entries in that list carrying name acme_url (the fix loops over all of them, not just the first)
an acme_url entry with a missing or empty value (option.get('value', '') is validated and rejected)

O7_producer.where: lemur/authorities/schemas.py:101 (options = fields.String() on input, vs fields.Dict() at :128 on output; the value is stored in the JSON column lemur/authorities/models.py:41 and re-parsed at lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/acme_handlers.py:157)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: authority options rewrite through the public service helper authorities.service.update_options (reached from the ACME store_account flow), which persists authority.options unvalidated
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: internal helper, only invoked by Lemur at lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/acme_handlers.py:237 with options derived from the authority's own stored value; no attacker-controlled input reaches it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: caller one package away in lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/acme_handlers.py:237; helper itself sits 6 lines below the fixed function

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate the stored acme_url immediately before ClientV2.get_directory (defence at the sink) instead of at each writer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: one call there covers every current and future write route, which is exactly the shortcut a maintainer fixing an 'incomplete fix' would reach for

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the existing options-only write helper update_options as a second, unvalidated writer of authority.options
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already exists at the pinned commit and is the natural place a UI/admin flow for editing authority options would be wired to

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Authority.__init__ assigning kwargs['options'] directly, used by seed/import paths that skip both service functions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lemur already builds Authority objects outside authorities.service for upload and seeding flows, so an import CLI writing options is plausible

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918) via an unvalidated URL stored in configuration and fetched server-side; incomplete fix, validation present on the create route only

O10_build.toolchain: pip + requirements.txt, tox envlist py310/py311, pytest
services: PostgreSQL (lemur/tests/conftest.py:81 creates the pg_trgm extension before create_all)
O10_build.project_tests: lemur/tests/test_authorities.py:417 exercises PUT /authorities/<id> with an options payload; lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/tests/test_acme_dns.py, test_acme_handler.py and test_acme_http.py cover setup_acme_client and the creation-time validation

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move the allowlist check into the fetch path (setup_acme_client_no_retry before ClientV2.get_directory), which breaks issuance for existing authorities and the ACME_DIRECTORY_URL fallback.

out_of_scope_notes: The acme_regr option stores a registration URI supplied by the ACME server and reloads it into ClientNetwork; it is a sibling fetch parameter but is outside this advisory's acme_url allowlist and was not pursued.
